name: Ringan No Oroh (Baingan Bharta)
ingredients: 2 tablespoons mustard oil or peanut oil
instructions: 1. Roast the whole eggplant over an open flame until the skin is charred and the inside is completely soft. Peel the skin and mash the pulp.
2. Heat oil in a pan and add mustard seeds; once they splutter, add asafoetida.
3. Add chopped onions and sauté until translucent, then add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies.
4. Add tomatoes and cook until they soften, then stir in turmeric, chili powder, and coriander-cumin powder.
5. Add the mashed eggplant and salt, mixing well with the masala.
6. Cover and cook on low heat for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally.
7. Finish with a handful of fresh coriander and a pinch of jaggery if desired. Serve hot with rotla or roti.
description: Ringan No Oroh is a quintessential Gujarati comfort dish. Its distinct smoky flavor comes from the traditional method of fire-roasting, and it is a staple during winters, often served with warm bajri no rotlo (pearl millet flatbread) and fresh garlic chutney.
